title: Match one plant to its actual growing conditions

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Plant care depends on identified species, medium, light and actual guidance. One symptom can have multiple causes; watering on a schedule alone cannot diagnose the need. A growing cycle includes preparation, establishment, monitoring and an appropriate end or harvest, not only one watering.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Fictional supplier trial card for a nonfood ornamental seed: use the supplied clean medium and labeled container in bright indirect light; check the surface daily; add a small amount of water only when the card’s stated dry-surface condition is present, avoiding standing water. The packet gives germination 7–14 days; no fertilizer/pesticide instruction. Day 3 surface is wet; day 8 still wet with no shoot. Species identity/toxicity for a real home is not supplied, so this is a paper case only.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Compare wetness, time window and missing identification. Plan the next observation and a supplier question rather than diagnosing or adding treatments.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: Two plants have yellow leaves, one with dry medium and one persistently wet. Is a single automatic watering remedy justified?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Day 8 lies within the supplied germination window; lack of a shoot is not alone failure. Continued wetness gives no basis to add more water under this card. Ask about the actual medium/drainage and identification before a live trial. Partial: wait but ignore wetness. Incorrect: add pesticide or declare disease. Next record germination date, establishment and later condition under an identified plant’s guidance, with a planned responsible end to the trial.
criteria: Care follows an identified applicable guide
A cycle has observations beyond one action

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. The same appearance does not establish the same cause or treatment. Check species-specific guidance and actual conditions; retain uncertainty and seek suitable expertise instead of escalating products.
